name: Drought
value: El Niño drought cuts Sudan harvest outlook
summary: El Niño drought hits Sudan's harvest and crops in Asia and Central America; no drought-driven famine declared
state: FAO says below-average rains linked to El Niño left severe drought on up to 70% of cropland in Gedaref and 55% in Sennar, with Sudan's harvest starting in November (FAO GIEWS, 24 Sep). Reuters reported that July–September rainfall was the lowest in over 30 years and that the IPC warned on 12 Oct of growing famine risk in conflict areas (TimesLIVE, 23 Oct). Searches on 28 Nov found no drought-driven famine declaration and no major exporter's harvest failure, so Watch holds.
for_you: People in Sudan, the Horn of Africa and parts of South-East Asia are most exposed to lower harvests and higher local food prices. Drought in several producing regions at once tends to tighten global grain supplies.
rubric_hit: Watch: severe drought in a major crop region (Gedaref up to 70% of cropland, FAO); no famine declared

sources.title: TimesLIVE (Reuters) — New famine risk haunts war-torn Sudan with El Niño-driven drought

why: Drought slowly destroys harvests, hydropower and river shipping, and drives famine and migration.
drivers: Rainfall deficits, heat, ENSO, groundwater depletion.

rubric.alert: Drought driving famine conditions, a major exporter's harvest failure, or monsoon failure across a major breadbasket.
rubric.watch: Severe drought in a major crop region, a major river at record low, or a monsoon running more than 20% below normal.
rubric.normal: No major breadbasket in severe drought.
